svg.text: Token-Based Integration on WSO2: Our Implementation
SevaOne takes the Seva Sindhu role. Departments change nothing. WSO2 Identity Server and API Manager carry the token, the callback and the status check.
Logs in with OTP or DigiLocker
TLS · routes portal and API traffic
Creates the unique edcsApplicationRefNo and asks WSO2 Identity
Server for the Token. Builds the auto-submitting POST form:
Takes the call that the gateway has already screened. Checks the
Token with WSO2 Identity Server, matches it to the stored handoff and
the department, saves the payment and acknowledgement once,
sets SUCCESS, and answers in the contract's format.
Asks each department or Sakala (GSE) for the status of an
application by GSC number, through the gateway.
Login: citizen, operator and admin issuers (already in place)
Mints the Token: OAuth2 access token for each handoff, with the
department and service in its scope. Opaque, single use, 30 minutes.
Introspection: is the Token active, and for which department?
Revocation: the Token is revoked after a successful URL 2 save.
Kill switch: disable a department's account or app, effect is live.
and JSON as the contract. Checks Basic credentials, IP allow-list,
throttle tier per department and payload size. Stamps the gateway secret.
Outbound APIs: one per department for URL 3. Retry, timeout and
throttling live here. Analytics and a department application for each.
Optional: a Token-check API backed by IS introspection.

Accepts the POST form and answers HTTP 200.
No change: this is what Seva Sindhu sends today.

The citizen fills the form and pays on the department's site
Generates the acknowledgement and posts it with Basic auth.
Calls again if SevaOne answers "Data Not Inserted".

Provided by the department, or by Sakala (GSE).
Looks an application up by GSC number.
